html:
The Teslin Tlingit are an inland Tlingit people of Teslin Lake, which straddles the border between Yukon and British Columbia. This map territory is the British Columbia part of their land; see Teslin Tlingit Council (Yukon).

Their ancestors moved inland from the coast of Lingít Aaní and mixed with Athabaskan Tagish neighbours, trading coastal goods for furs. The Alaska Highway, built in 1942, passed through the village of Teslin. Under the Yukon land claims agreements of the 1990s the Teslin Tlingit Council became a self governing First Nation. Their kin to the south are the Taku River Tlingit.
